profile.campus: Settimo Milanese, greater Milan, Italy (Equinix ML5)
profile.address: Via Marisa Bellisario 5, 20019 Settimo Milanese, Italy
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's ML5 facility at Via Marisa Bellisario 5 in Settimo Milanese, a short distance from sibling facility ML7x on the same street. Equinix's own dedicated page describes ML5 as a three-story, reinforced-concrete building with 4,200 square meters, about 45,208 square feet, of colocation space, the largest confirmed figure among the international facilities in this registry, sited next to Via Caldera, which Equinix's page describes as the most well-connected location in Milan. Equinix states ML5 connects directly to its Genoa GN1 facility, functioning together as a subsea cable hub for the Mediterranean region, reflecting Genoa's status as a major Italian port for transcontinental submarine cables. The page states N+1 power and cooling redundancy and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current ML5 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.
